phase_0.boundary_condition: The covalent ring closure of the monosaccharide, which kinetically freezes the configuration and prevents spontaneous rearrangement without enzymatic catalysis.

⊢.justification: The open-chain aldehyde or ketone form before cyclization, representing the void state before the ring structure is established.

⊣.justification: The hemiacetal or hemiketal bond that seals the ring, acting as the terminal anchor that contains the entire sugar topology.

≻.justification: The forward morphism of adding a sugar residue to a growing chain, driven by the reactivity of the anomeric hydroxyl group.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism of breaking a glycosidic bond, representing descent or decomposition of the structure.

⋈.justification: The sequential chaining of monosaccharides via O-glycosidic bonds, transmitting stereochemical geometry and information content.

⊙.justification: The self-recognition of the ring system (6-membered pyranose or 5-membered furanose) as a stable, self-referential unit.

∈.justification: The anomeric carbon splits into two distinct stereochemical arms: alpha (axial) and beta (equatorial) configurations.

∋.justification: The rejoining of alpha and beta arms into a single dynamic equilibrium state, or a fixed state if locked by a glycosidic bond.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state of the hydroxyl group acting as an acid (EVALT), donating a proton or participating in hydrogen bonding as a donor.

⊥.justification: The negative state of the N-acetyl amine group acting as a base (EVALF), accepting a proton or serving as a hydrogen bond acceptor.

⊞.justification: The paradice state where a chiral center holds both R and S potential simultaneously in the transition state, or where a sugar exhibits dual donor/acceptor roles.

◻.justification: The irreversible fixation of the glycosidic bond, which locks the anomeric configuration and prevents thermal interconversion.

phase_3.void_description: The open-chain aldehyde/ketone precursor before cyclization.
phase_3.true_description: The alpha-anomer configuration (axial) or the beta-anomer configuration (equatorial) when exclusively stabilized.
phase_3.false_description: The refuted anomer configuration when the other is locked, or the absence of a specific functional group interaction.
phase_3.both_description: The mutarotation equilibrium where alpha and beta forms coexist, or a chiral center holding dual potential in a transition state.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the acyclic sugar precursor (aldehyde/ketone) in the void state.
Drive the cyclization reaction forward via nucleophilic attack of a hydroxyl on the carbonyl.
Seal the ring with the hemiacetal/hemiketal bond, establishing the boundary.
Recognize the ring identity (pyranose or furanose) as a self-contained unit.
Split the anomeric carbon into alpha and beta stereochemical arms.
Evaluate the alpha-arm: hydroxyl groups act as acids (donors) and ring oxygen as acceptor.
Evaluate the beta-arm: N-acetyl groups (in GlcNAc/GalNAc) act as bases (acceptors).
Hold the chiral center in a paradice state where both R/S potentials are active during transition.
Rejoin the alpha and beta arms into a single equilibrium state (B) or a locked state (T/F).
Chain the monosaccharide to the next via a glycosidic bond, transmitting stereochemical fidelity.
Irreversibly fix the glycosidic bond, freezing the anomeric configuration and preventing rearrangement.
Allow for hydrolysis (reverse morphism) only if enzymatic catalysis is present, otherwise the bond remains fixed.
Re-assert the identity of the now-linked disaccharide or oligosaccharide unit.
Anchor the entire glycan tree at the reducing end, completing the boundary interface.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The functional group grammar (SMARTS patterns) that maps chemical structures to IMASM opcodes.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Hydrogen bonding networks and steric interactions between sugar residues.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The covalent glycosidic bonds that store the sequence and stereochemistry of the glycan.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The ordered sequence of enzymatic additions (glycosyltransferases) that dictate the growth of the glycan tree.
phase_5.alfs_store: The set of mammalian N-glycan monosaccharides (GlcNAc, GalNAc, Mannose, Galactose, Glucose, Fucose, Sialic acid, Xylose) and their functional group signatures.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Activation energy required for glycosyltransferase catalysis and the entropic cost of ordering the sugar residues.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: A disordered mixture of monosaccharide precursors and lipid carriers.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A highly ordered, branched glycan tree with specific stereochemistry and functional group orientation.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The system is entropy-conservative because the covalent fixation (IFIX) of the glycosidic bonds locks the configuration, preventing thermal interconversion and maintaining the ordered state without continuous energy input.
